# SeqPhaseColumns4

Phases side by side, with today's one marked.

## When to use it

Three or four phases with long activity lists, and it matters which phase the client is in now.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | C-sequence (secondary B-enumeration) |
| Form | phases |
| Arity | 4 |
| Ground | cream, alt |
| Density | dense, about 1420 characters |
| Media | none |
| Focal | phaseName at 30px against a 64px headline (ratio 0.47) |

## Why it holds together

Low, and the real emphasis is the tint on the current column — ground, not size.

## Deviations from the traced source

| What | Source | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| my own index note | says the slide has no time axis and one must be added | ordinals, not a drawn axis | Half right. A ruled axis implies durations the source does not carry and nobody has measured; numbering gives the sequence without inventing data. |

Copy only. The geometry is measured off a real slide, so when you rebuild it in Claude Design Slides keep the positions and sizes in the preview exactly: change the words, not the grid. Build the text and shapes from the Elements cards, each of which ends with its Slides recipe.

# SeqStepsPanels5

Five-stage method with substance under each stage.

## When to use it

A method of four or five stages where each stage has real activities and deliverables to name.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | C-sequence |
| Form | steps |
| Arity | 5 |
| Ground | cream, navy |
| Density | dense, about 1450 characters |
| Media | none |
| Focal | headline at 64px against a 64px headline (ratio 1.0) |

## Why it holds together

Flat by design. Nothing competes with the headline because the panels are doing volume, not display. A giant ordinal here would fight 45 lines of second-level copy.

## Related kit layout

`ProcessTimelineV1` — ProcessTimelineV1 has no second level at all, so a five-stage method with real substance flattens to five one-line cards. Do not retire it until this has been through a real deck — v1 is still right when the stages genuinely are one-liners.

## Deviations from the traced source

| What | Source | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| chevron step headers | arrow-tipped | flat with a rule | Unsanctioned ornament, and redundant with the ordinal and reading order. |
| panel heights | ragged, first panel clipped mid-word | equal, centred | The source ran out of room. Reproducing that would be copying a defect. |

Copy only. The geometry is measured off a real slide, so when you rebuild it in Claude Design Slides keep the positions and sizes in the preview exactly: change the words, not the grid. Build the text and shapes from the Elements cards, each of which ends with its Slides recipe.
